    - Eat regular meals (3 main meals, 1-2 snacks) to avoid large fluctuations in blood sugar.
    - Prioritise high-fibre, low-glycaemic carbohydrates (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, berries, apples).
    - Include lean protein at every meal (e.g. eggs, fish, poultry, tofu, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese).
    - Include healthy fats (e.g. olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds) in moderation.
    - Fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables (e.g. leafy greens, broccoli, peppers, zucchini).
    - Limit added sugars and refined grains (e.g. white bread, pastries, sugary drinks).
    - Stay hydrated: aim for at least 1.5-2L water daily.
    - Avoid skipping meals to reduce risk of under-fuelling and blood sugar dips.
    - Consider a bedtime snack with protein and fibre if prone to overnight hypoglycaemia.
    - Monitor energy, mood, cycle, and recovery; increase intake if feeling fatigued, irritable, or under-recovered.

  FOCUS glycaemic_control
  GUIDELINES
    - Aggressive calorie restriction is not recommended for PCOS due to risk of under-fuelling, hormonal disruption, and worsening metabolic health.
    - Minimum daily intake: 1500 kcal unless supervised by a registered dietitian or physician.
    - Eat regular meals (3 main meals, 1-2 snacks) to avoid large fluctuations in blood sugar.
    - Prioritise high-fibre, low-glycaemic carbohydrates (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, berries, apples).
    - Include lean protein at every meal (e.g. eggs, fish, poultry, tofu, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese).
    - Include healthy fats (e.g. olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds) in moderation.
    - Fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables (e.g. leafy greens, broccoli, peppers, zucchini).
    - Limit added sugars and refined grains (e.g. white bread, pastries, sugary drinks).
    - Stay hydrated: aim for at least 1.5-2L water daily.
    - Avoid skipping meals to reduce risk of under-fuelling and blood sugar dips.
    - Consider a bedtime snack with protein and fibre if prone to overnight hypoglycaemia.
    - Monitor energy, mood, cycle, and recovery; increase intake if feeling fatigued, irritable, or under-recovered.
    - If possible, consult a registered dietitian for individualised support and safe calorie targets.
